mechanism: Compare red square objects (three) with blue white unit-square objects (ten), transferring shape correspondence across scale. Intended error is 3:10 by counting the large gray square as one unit instead of four. All gray fills, original square sizes and square boundaries remain unchanged.
mathematical_solution: Use any small square as area unit u. Ten white squares have area 10u. The central gray square has twice a small square side, hence area 4u; the two other gray squares have area u each. Gray:white = (4+1+1):10 = 3:5, uniquely D. Appearance colors mark square identity without asserting congruence, and the 2:1 side ratio remains plainly visible.
